defects.detail: 'Master Fanyun Wanhui' for 萬迴法雲公 (Fayun)

spans.why: source has 法雲 (Fayun), not Fanyun
僧伽 is Sengqie; 'Songga' is a wrong romanisation
the page opens scroll 27 with its title; nothing carries over

spans.quote: He wore a pair of scissors, a ruler, and a bronze mirror on his head
spans.why: 頭擐 refers to items hung from the staff head; read as worn on his own head

invention.quote: <note>meaning they did not occupy official abbacy positions to teach public assemblies</note>

defects.detail: 'Lord Fayuan of Wanhui' for 萬迴法雲公: Wanhui is the person, Fayun his title

spans.why: 萬迴法雲公 is Wanhui, Lord Fayun; name misread and structure inverted

spans.quote: At the beginning of the Taisishi era
From his head hung scissors, a ruler, and a copper mirror
spans.why: 頭擐 refers to items hung from the staff head; read as his own head

reason: Both render the title, the ten-name list, 諸方雜舉徵拈代別語 and Baozhi's life to 忽一日重 in full; each garbles one or two names (T1 'Fanyun', 'Songga'; T2 'Fayuan of Wanhui', 'Taisishi'), and T2's date notes (465, 489) are correct.

<note>Guan Yunshi (1286–1324), a famous Yuan dynasty poet and musician</note>

spans.why: 篳篥 (bili) rendered as 'oboe'; it is glossed in a note, but the term is anachronistic

defects.detail: 'I lie in hills and valleys' for 眼空湖海臥丘壑, which describes Xiying

spans.quote: With eyes empty of lakes and seas, I lie in hills and valleys,
spans.why: the lines describe Xiying; the speaker 'I' is introduced only at 我訪

spans.quote: Accustomed to laziness, I intend to keep an appointment with the clouds.
spans.why: same misattribution of the subject to the poet

reason: Both cover 覩其毫絲 to 吹者之妙 in full; T2 makes the poet the subject of 眼空湖海臥丘壑，習懶擬與雲相期, which describe Xiying; T1 reads it correctly and its Guan Yunshi note is right.

invention.quote: A woodcut depicts a pelican feeding her young from her own breast

defects.detail: invented note 'a pelican feeding her young ... alchemical tradition'; the page is plain Chan text with no image
'Gauda's single finger' for 俱胝一指 (Juzhi)

spans.quote: A woodcut depicts a pelican feeding her young from her own breast
spans.why: no such image on the page; a fabricated note from another book

spans.quote: At the invitation of Inspector Geng
spans.why: the source has 趙觀察, Inspector Zhao

spans.quote: the ocean of perfumed water floats the banner-like stupa
spans.why: 浮幢剎 (floating world-systems in the fragrant ocean) garbled

defects.detail: 'drop a ten-thousand-mile hook to halt the thousand-mile black steed' joins 垂萬里鉤 and 駐千里烏騅 as means and end

spans.quote: to catch the fish that leap through the waves, and drop a ten-thousand-mile hook to halt
spans.why: the source lists parallel feats (布漫天網，打衝浪魚，垂萬里鉤，駐千里烏騅); recast as purpose clauses

spans.quote: When one is direct and unclouded in the sunlight
spans.why: 當陽直截 means 'facing it directly', not 'in the sunlight'

reason: T1 opens with an invented note about a pelican woodcut and misnames 趙觀察 as 'Geng' and 俱胝 as 'Gauda'; T2 keeps the names right, with only the parallel list 布漫天網…駐千里烏騅 recast as purpose clauses.
